newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major development in the air cargo industry in the week November 1 to November 8th.
**NOVEMBER 1**
LONDON - British trucking companies which service the air cargo industry are imposing five percent fuel surcharges from November 1 to counter the impact of higher diesel fuel costs.
SINGAPORE - Freight Links Express Holdings have entered into a conditional agreement to buy 8.15 million shares in Caxton Holdings for A$5.5 million from Eftus Investments Pty Ltd.
MOSCOW - Russia AO Aviastar aircraft manufacturer to resume work Nov 3 after 10-week stoppage caused by financial problems.
PARIS - Air France is considering increasing passenger fares on flights from France from November 4, but new rates yet to be finalised.
ZURICH - Swissair cutting fares to 32 destinations in 18 mainly European countries, for flights between November 8 and December 8 by around 50 percent.
LONDON - MSAS has appointed Teresa Vitch as managing director of its Spanish operating company.
*MSAS gains ISO 9002 award for all forwarding services from Madrid.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines Corp said its Canadian International unit had Q3 net income of C$85.7 million bringing losses for first nine months of 1996 to a worse than planned C$49 million
*CAL, struggling for survival amind heavy losses says it would transfer capacity, seek wage cuts from employees and ask for concessions from U.S. shareholder American Airlines.
FORTH WORTH - American Airlines says it remains committed to its stake in Canadian Airlines but does not plan any further investment in the ailing carrier.
LONDON, European jet prices tumbled on back of falling IPE gas oil, futures.
HONG KONG - Asiana airlines is increasing its ex-Seoul cargo rates by five percent from November 1 because of peak season demand and higher fuel prices.
AMSTERDAM - The Dutch ministry of transport is investigating an incident where an El Al freighter was flown just 260 metres over Amsterdam.
WASHINGTON - Strong demand for commerical aircraft drove new orders to U.S. factories higher during September.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines, struggling to survive amid heavy losses, plans to increase flights to the U.S., negotiate wage cuts and seek concessions from U.S. shareholders AMR Corp.
OTTAWA - Canadian transport minisdter welcomes Canadian Airlines tought measures to control costs.
HONG KONG - El Al to use 747 in place of 767 on Tel Aviv/Hkg route to increase cargo capacity and tourism.
SAO PAULO - Federal investigation begins into cause of Fokker-100 crash which killed at least 104 people on Nov 1.
LONDON - European airlines led the way in introducing 10 US cent a kg cargo fuel surcharge.
FORT WORTH - American Air's Oct load factor up 2.9 percent to 69.0 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch government optimistic on Samsung Aerospace's rescue package for Dutch Fokker planemaker. Earlier major suppliers indicated they were willing to wait a few more days for a poossible rescue.
LOS ANGELES - Boeing Co shares fell three pointsd to 92-3/8 after it said development of next generation of 747s could cost as much as $7 billion.
NEW YORK -USAir rates strong buy by Salomon Brother after cutting costs.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines' biggest union rejects carrier's survival plan based on lower wages.
FORT WORTH - American Airlines to implement 10 cent/kg fuel surcharge effective Nov 15 on most routes.
SEATTLE - Boeing recommends tests of rudder power controls on its 737s.
NEW YORK - U.S. airlines face minimal costs to comply with safety changes needed for Boeing 737s.
DALLAS - Southwest Airlines cuts 7-day advance purchase fares for many flights Dec 3 to April 4, 1997.
**November 2**
MANILA - Phillipine Airlines ground crew end three-day strike returning to work Sunday.
LONDON - BA checking over next few days on Boeing 737 rudder systems.
**November 3**
TAIPEI - A Taiwan cabinet panel has proposed building a T$10 billion airport town in northern county of Taoyuan.
GENEVA - New directions for air industry expected to be under discussion at this week's IATA AGM here.
ZURICH - Swissair chief says will not abandon Belgian partner carrier Sabena.
SEATTLE - Boeing may ask airlines to install rudder limiterson its 737s.
**November 4**
SYDNEY - Quantas had 37.7 percent of international passenger market in and out of Australia for year to end-July.
*Quantas completes checks on 737s without finding faults.
*Australian airlines Quantas and Ansett have no plans to impose fuel surcharge on cargo or passenger fares.
HONG KONG- Macau International airport said both passenger and cargo traffic in October set new records.

TORONTO - Canadian Airlines fuel surcharges of C12 cents/kg on international flights and C5cents/kg on domestic ones effective Nov 25. Air Canada expected to start westbound North Atlantic surcharges Nov 15 equivalent to US$0.10/kg.
DUBAI - Emirates airline said it is to buy 16 Airbus A330-200s with option for 7 more replacing A310 and A300 from 1999 to 2002.
*Dubai airport cargo volumes rose 13 percent in October to 32,082 tonnes from 28,314 tonnes in the same month last year, Dubai Cargo Village figures show.
*Lufthansa's Oct quality report for cargo handling at Sharjah show handling targets mainly met.
GENEVA - IATA head says airlines soaring fuel bills eating into airlines revenues but profits still heading for second successive record year.
VIENNA - Tyrolean Airways raising prices by average three percent effective Nov 4 because of fuel costs.
JOHANNESBURG - SAS introduciung air cargo surcharge from S Africa of 0.50 rand/kg effective Nov 15 and of US$0.10/kg ex-S Africa.
GENEVA - Air Transport Action Group (ATAG)said world industry employed 24 million in 1994 or 2 million more than in 1992./
RABAT - Morocco's Royal Air Maroc ordered two Boeing 737-800s for April 1998 delivery.

AMSTERDAM - Nippon Cargo Airline, the Japanese all-cargo airline, is likely to implement a fuel surcharge from the Netherlands shortly, said Gino Laan, a marketing executive with the airline based in Amsterdam.O ....ISTANBUL - Shares representing 15 percent capital of Turkish airport ground handling firm Celebi Hava Servisi A.S will be offered to the public on November 7-8.
BRUSSELS - Major European airlines carried six pct more passengers in Sept than Sept 1995, AEA figures showed.
LONDON - Rolls Royce signs MOU with Airbus consortium specifying its Trent 900 as engine for the planned new A3XX large capacity airliner.
GENEVA - IATA said at AGM it would launch judicial challenge to new British law on lower noise limits for aircraft taking off from London airports from Jan one.
*Lufthansa and Swissair plan to lift passenger airfares due to rising fuel costs, following earlier increases for air cargo, top executives told a news conference but set no date for the increase.
*American Airlines chairman said its fuel bills so far this year have risen $300-400 million because of high jet fuel prices.
*AA chief said expects regulatory approval for its tie-up with BA by end-March 1997.
ATLANTA - ValuJet realigns management structiure and names D Joseph Carr prfesident and chief executive from Nov 6.
NEW YORK - Gulfstream listed as strong buy by Morgan Stanley and recommended by Goldman Sachs.
PARIS, Nov 4 (Reuter) - France's association of air freight forwarding agents, SNAGFA, said the way surcharges on freight had been applied, to cover rising jet fuel costs, was totally "unacceptable.
*Air France increase prices because of fuel costs.
MAASTRICHT, Nov 4 (Reuters) - The Dutch Cabinet has approved a limited expansion of the country's most southerly airport, a Ministry of Transport spokesman said.
NEW YORK - Federal Express shares rally on news it will add 20 Chinese cities a year to delivery area over next five years.
*Investigators seeking the cause of the TWA Flight 800 disaster begin dredging part of the crash site.
CALGARY - Analysts said Canadian Airlines rescue plan falls short of addressing the cash drain caused by domestic overcapacity.
MEXICO CITY - Two Mexican states are trying to convince the federal government where to locate a second airport for Mexico City.
ZURICH - Global cargo traffic handled at Zurich Jan-Sept totalled 325,482 tonnes, down 0.9 percent on the same period last year, airport authority figures show.
PARIS - French TAT airline union representing attendents calls one day strike for Nov 5 in protest at staffing levels.
**November 5**
KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysian Airlines begins checking rudsders on its Boeing 737s.
SANTIAGO - Linea Area de Chile agree to cede to competing Chuilean airline National seven of its 28 weekly round-trip flights between Santiago and the U.S..
BEIJING -China signs agreement to buy passenger engines from CFM Inter in $130 million deal.
SYDNEY - Ansett airline reports operating loss of A$18.6 million in year to June 30, 1996.
*Quantas says foreign shareholders now hold 50.29 pct of airline.
LONDON - BA half year profit up 9.3 pct to 470 million stg but would have been higher but for fuel price rise.
*In October BA cargo carried was 333 million tonnes/kms vs 310 and total passengers carried rose 4.7 pct to 3.017 million.
*BA chief executive remains hopeful that proposed link with American Airlines will be approved.
*BA receives more dividends on $400 mil;lion investment in USAir Group.
Airbuas vice-presiodent John leahy said BA seriously interested in proposed Airbus A3XX-100 super jumbo.
FRANKFURT - Thai airlines set fuel surcharge from
PARIS - Commercial courts say Air Liberte does not need to be wound down and lawyers said this opens way for BA and Banque Rivaud to buy firm.
LONDON - BA says its bid for Air Liberte accepted but in Paris commercial court describes this statement as excessive as nothing to stop any other bid.
WASHINGTON - U.S. and U.K. to start new talks Nov 6 to forge open skies pact ending restrictions on aiur traffic.
ARLINGTON, Va - USAir Group October load factor 69.9 pct vs 67.5 pct year ago.
NEW YORK - Airbus will price proposed 550 seat A3XX superjumbo at $198 million a senior company official said in a Wall Street Journal interview.
BRUSSELS - Daimler-Benz Aerospace predicts Airbus order would almost triplein 1996 compared with 1995.
NICOSIA - Cyprus Airways 2.9 million stg loss in 1st half 1996 loss reflecting high fuel costs and a crisis in tourism.
MANILA - Philippines report 16.6 pct hike in merchandise exports in Jan-Sept at US$14.926 billion with electronics and components accouting for 40.9 pct of receipts.
LONDON - Canadian Airlines carried 44.8 million cargo tonne miles in October or 1.2 million more than previous month and unchanged from October last year.
PARIS - Air France has cut flying time to Seooul by two hours 35 minutes after China allowed it to fly over Beijing area.
BRUSSELS - EU commission head Santer said U.S. interference in favour of civil and military sales could distort global aerospace market.
STOCKHOLM - SAS said it and United airines given U.S. Dept of Transport antitrust immunity for their marketing alliance.

*A Reuter survey showed air cargo rates from Stockholm to the Far East showed signs of firming over the past month but those to Europe and South America fell when eyes were focusing on whether all carriers would impose fuel surcharges.

LUXEMBOURG - Cargolux said Sept's 176.7 million freight tonne kilometres was nine percent up on year ago. ....ALMATY - Kazakhstan and Japan plan to start regular fligfhts between new Kazak capital of Askmola and Tokyo but gave no more details.
NEW YORK - Mesa Air October load factor up 2.5 pct to 56.8 pct from year ago.
AMSTERDAM - KLM first half profit up 21 pct to 529 million guilders but Q2 prtofit down 14 pct after fuel costs were about 125 guilder higher.
*KLM unveils cost cutting and restructuring drive drive aimed at savings of at least 1.5 billion guilders over three years when revealing results
*KLM suspends expansion of European fleet as part of cost cutting drive.
*KLM said cargo capacity growth has slowed and now within range of cargo traffic growth.
HONG KONG - Chine signs US$1.7 billion agreement with European consortium Aero International to build 100 seater passenger plane
*Eleven arrested at Schiphol on changes of theft from warehouses operated by Avio Presto.
SYDNEY - Dutch KPN group increases stake in TNT to 19.2 pct following market purchase of more than 13 million shares.
LONDON, Granada sells its 25 percent share in Alpha Airports Group for 52.6 million stg to a firm owned by MohamedAl Fayed.
*Rolls Royce expects to get about $150 million from Asian order for V2500 engines.
*Emery Worldwide has opened a new service centre at Newcastle airport in NE England.
PARIS - Sweden's Saab wants to join Airbus consortium in the future A3XX superjumbo project.
*Emirates Air;ine adds Sanaa and Kuala Lumpur to its ex-France winter timetable with stopovers in Dubai in both directions.
*Corsaid applied to French authorities for landing rights in Madagasy and Comoros Islands.
COPENHAGEN - SAS cut all Copenhagen-Brussels fares after Virgin complained at selective cuts.
GOTHENBURG - Crgolux calls for intergrated air freioght system made up of airlines, forwarders and ground handlers.

**NOVEMBER 6** BANGKOK - Nearly 1,500 Thai Airways cargo workers return to work ending a two-day strikethat delayed vital parts for sdome industries. Strike was in protest over government decision to allow new cargo carrier to be launched as this couldjeop BANGKOK, Nov 4 (Reuter) - Cargo handling workers of Thai Airways International Plc started a strike at Bangkok's Don Muang airport on Monday to press their demand for the government to overturn its decision to launch a new Thai cargo airline.
SANAA - BA offered Yemen and Aden landing rights on last leg of British foreign secretary's (foreign minister's) visit.
